clue.text: Crimean heroine clearly needed a hurricane lamp

definitions.meaning: Florence, the nurse famed for her work in the Crimean War
a dark, stormy time when a storm lantern is wanted

explanation.walkthrough: The second half splits as NIGHT IN GALE: after dark in a storm you would certainly want a hurricane lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: The nurse who tended soldiers at Scutari became the celebrated heroine of the Crimean War.

clue.text: Central pub about to be erected

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: in a down clue, erected means set upright, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A bar in the middle of town is about to be built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be erected' only works because this is a down clue: standing a word upright means reading it from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inner lies at the centre, so central is a synonym.

clue.text: Self-important chap of prime importance to a calligrapher!

definitions.meaning: a mock title for a pompous man

definitions.text: of prime importance to a calligrapher!
definitions.meaning: a penman's pen points would be his most vital tools

explanation.definitionFit: The jocular title mocks a man with airs; literally, a pen-and-ink artist cannot work without his pen points.

clue.text: Not out of the team

definitions.meaning: within, not outside; also slang for in prison
split: a member of the side picked

explanation.definitionFit: The word means within rather than without, and broken in two it says in the side, i.e. selected for the team.

clue.text: Dogma one disseminated to gain a reputation

indicators.note: spread around widely, so the letters of the two words are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Spreading one's doctrine to earn renown.
explanation.definitionFit: A good name is the standing others credit one with, which is what reputation means.

clue.text: Leaning over a computer print-out

definitions.meaning: tilting to one side, as a ship does
a printed list of program code or data

explanation.definitionFit: A ship that lists tilts to one side; a printed record of data or code from a machine is also called by this word.

clue.text: A hypodermic needle is the last thing one will accept

definitions.meaning: humorously, the sharp tip that does the jabbing

definitions.text: the last thing one will accept
definitions.meaning: an issue on which one refuses to give way in a negotiation

explanation.definitionFit: Literally a sharp tip that jabs; figuratively an obstacle in talks where neither side will concede.

clue.text: Petty officer who is an apple-lover?

parts.note: a Cox, short for Cox's Orange Pippin, is a common British eating apple
a swain is an old word for a suitor or lover

explanation.surface: A naval rating who is mad about apples.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cox is a popular British apple variety; read 'apple-lover' as COX plus SWAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The helmsman who steers a ship's boat is traditionally a petty officer in the navy.

clue.text: Costers on the open market

definitions.meaning: costermongers, barrow-sellers of fruit and vegetables
cryptically, people selling out on the road

explanation.walkthrough: Costermongers were London barrow-boys who sold fruit and vegetables from street stalls.
explanation.definitionFit: Costermongers are hawkers who sell from barrows on public roads; the second part pictures selling in the open air.

clue.text: A great deal of wine is Mediterranean port

parts.note: a tun is a huge cask holding a vast amount of wine
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lots of wine flows at a busy Mediterranean harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Tunisia is a seaport on the North African Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Pull up quickly to remedy a current fault

definitions.meaning: halt suddenly
to end an electrical short circuit

explanation.definitionFit: To halt abruptly; read literally, to put an end to a short circuit in an electric current.

clue.text: Continued-with a love affair, presumably

definitions.meaning: kept going
conducting a romantic liaison, as in 'having an affair'

explanation.definitionFit: Went on doing something; also the idiom for conducting an illicit romance.

clue.text: Hand-out for the children

definitions.meaning: to distribute, give out supplies
offspring, as in dying without heirs

explanation.definitionFit: To distribute something officially; also a legal word for one's offspring.

clue.text: I am to get a job out of duty

parts.note: contracted to I'm
a post is a position or job

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to find work out of a sense of obligation.
explanation.definitionFit: An impost is a tax or levy, i.e. a duty charged on goods.

clue.text: Sponger finds where airborne soldiers are based

parts.note: paras are parachute troops
a site is the place where something is based or located

explanation.surface: A freeloader turns up at the paratroopers' camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite lives off others, which is just what a sponger or freeloader does.

clue.text: Garment I designed for one going overseas

indicators.note: a garment that is designed is fashioned anew, so the letters are made into a new shape

explanation.surface: A tailor makes an outfit for someone travelling abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigrant leaves home to settle in another country, often across the sea.

clue.text: Feeble agent gets it after a month

indicators.note: after says the agent and it follow the month in the answer

parts.note: Dec is the short form of December
a rep is a sales agent, a representative
taken as written

explanation.surface: A weak representative obtains something a month later.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit describes someone worn out with age, frail and so feeble.

clue.text: He cultivates a Shakespearean forest in Germany

indicators.note: in says the forest's name is placed within the abbreviation for the country

parts.note: the Forest of Arden is the setting of As You Like It

explanation.surface: A man tends a woodland from Shakespeare that lies in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tends a plot of ground and grows plants is a horticulturist, one who cultivates.

clue.text: Cuttings in Early English put others in the shade

indicators.note: in says the cuttings are placed within the abbreviation

parts.note: clips are snippets or cuttings

explanation.surface: Snippets from early English texts overshadow everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: To outshine rivals is to surpass them, just as the moon blocks out the sun.

clue.text: Gather that 18 got disheartened

indicators.note: with its heart removed, so the middle letters of the referenced word are cut out

parts.note: refers to the answer at 18 across

explanation.surface: Collect what the horticulturist obtained after losing heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' removes the central DE of the 18-across word.
explanation.definitionFit: To garner is to collect up, especially a harvest, which is to gather.

clue.text: A theologian gets a sign from the lower regions

parts.note: taken as written
BD, Bachelor of Divinity, a degree held by a theologian
an omen is a portent or sign

explanation.surface: A divine receives a portent from the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the lower regions' suggests hell, but here it is the belly.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly is the lower part of the trunk, so the lower regions of the body.

clue.text: Paper quota ordered is about right

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters surround the abbreviation for right
the quota is put in order differently, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The amount of paper requisitioned is roughly correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges QUOTA into QUATO, which 'about' wraps round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarto is a sheet folded twice, and the name of that size of paper.

clue.text: Thrush found by a Sussex river and lake

parts.note: the Ouse flows through Sussex to the sea at Newhaven

explanation.surface: A songbird spotted beside a river and a lake in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The ring ouzel is a kind of thrush, and the word is also an old name for the blackbird.

clue.text: Moon-faced Parliamentarian

definitions.meaning: having a face as round as the full moon
a supporter of Parliament in the English Civil War

explanation.walkthrough: The Parliamentarians of the 1640s English Civil War were nicknamed for their cropped hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a person with a circular face; historically a Puritan soldier of Cromwell's side, named for his short haircut.

clue.text: Points Miss Lawley has to follow

parts.note: E and N are compass points: east and north
Sue Lawley, British broadcaster and former Desert Island Discs presenter

explanation.surface: A broadcaster must come after several points have been made.
explanation.walkthrough: Sue Lawley is a British TV and radio presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after as a result, i.e. to follow.

clue.text: Music manuscript used by correspondents

definitions.meaning: humorously, sheets for writing musical notes on
stationery for writing letters

explanation.definitionFit: Literally sheets for musical notation; actually the stationery people write letters on.

clue.text: A Miami sergeant is somewhat tight-fisted

definitions.note: adjective standing for a noun: one who is tight-fisted

indicators.note: somewhat suggests only part of the phrase is used, a run of letters within the words

explanation.surface: An American police sergeant is a bit stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is adjectival for a noun answer: read it as 'one who is tight-fisted'.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser hoards money and hates spending, the very picture of a stingy person.

clue.text: Retained barrister and refused to give an opinion

definitions.meaning: hired a lawyer to plead one's case
kept one's own views to oneself

explanation.definitionFit: Literally hired a lawyer; idiomatically stayed silent about one's thoughts.
